summary.text: A 57-year-old male with a BMI of 48.7 kg/m^(2) and asthma, coronary artery disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, ischemic cardiomyopathy, obstructive sleep apnea and hypothyroidism sustained bilateral pilon fractures, a T2 superior endplate fracture and bilateral pulmonary contusions in a motor vehicle collision. He presented to a regional hospital and was transferred 10 days after the injury.

Surgery occurred 2 days later: the left leg had an anterior approach with excision of joint fragments and plate fixation, and the right leg had a distal fibular plate and circular ring fixator removed 2 months later. He used a wheelchair, then crutches, and was compliant with restrictions.

One year after the initial surgery the left leg was reported healed without complications, though the Discussion reports left tibial nonunion. The right leg developed distal tibial nonunion with posttraumatic arthritis and underwent right ankle fusion, plate removal at 2.5 years and subtalar fusion at 3 years post-index surgery.

summary.text: A 38-year-old male with a BMI of 27.5 kg/m^(2) and a history of alcohol use disorder, paranoid schizophrenia, smoking and prior bilateral calcaneal fractures treated with ORIF 4 years earlier sustained bilateral pilon fractures after jumping from a third-story window. He presented to the hospital 5 days after injury.

Initial surgery 3 days after presentation involved left ORIF with locking plates and a right external fixator because of fracture blisters; right ORIF followed one week later. He was non-weightbearing in a wheelchair for 12 weeks and adhered poorly to restrictions.

He healed uneventfully for 2 years until a 15-foot fall caused a left bicondylar tibial plateau fracture and left tibial shaft fracture requiring ORIF of the left tibia. Pilon fracture hardware remained in proper alignment, and no complications were reported to the most recent follow-up.

summary.text: A 42-year-old male with a BMI of 33.7 kg/m^(2), asthma, marijuana use and vaping use presented after a 30-foot fall from a ladder at work with bilateral open pilon fractures, nondisplaced L2 and L3 transverse process fractures and a posterior right 12th rib fracture.

Initial surgery the same day placed lateral locking plates with a left anterior incision and bilateral spanning external fixators. Three days later the fixators were removed and definitive bilateral fixation performed. He was non-weightbearing in a wheelchair, with partial weightbearing and crutches at 12 weeks, and participated in physical therapy.

Left leg pain and distal tibial nonunion led to revision surgery with a posterior iliac crest bone graft, with timing differing between text and a figure caption. At 1.5 years he developed ongoing pain from post-traumatic arthritis and required right tibiotalar arthrodesis; radiographs at 1 year 9 months showed right ankle arthrodesis and a healed left ankle.
